answers.who: young people today who will still be alive in 2076 and have to live with decisions being made now about AI and governance
answers.broken: arguments about letting AI run things are loud, one-sided, and never show where a choice actually leads, so people have opinions but not odds
answers.changed: a tool called AI Runs the Planet that gives an AI (or a test audience) a budget of 360 points across six levers to simulate thousands of futures to 2076, showing best case, most likely, and worst case outcomes with disaster and breakthrough markers
answers.proof: the AI's allocation kept 92% of simulated futures below 2 degrees but resulted in 31 million people displaced by sea in the most likely future, versus a test audience's people-first allocation that only displaced 8 million but kept none of its futures below 2 degrees

answers.who: young people today who will still be living in the world in 2076, and anyone wanting to weigh in on how the planet's future is decided
answers.broken: people argue online about letting AI run governments but nobody has actual odds or data, and headlines are loud, one-sided, and don't show where a choice leads
answers.changed: a tool called AI Runs the Planet gives an AI the same budget as regular people (360 points across six levers: clean energy, carbon price, sea walls, food, working together, and tech), simulates thousands of futures to 2076, and shows the best case, most likely case, and scariest case so people can see odds before decisions are made, and compare AI's choices versus their own
answers.proof: the AI kept 92% of simulated futures below 2 degrees but only put 1 point into coastal protection, leading to 31 million people displaced by the sea in its most likely future; a test audience spending the same budget on people first only had 8 million displaced, but none of their futures stayed below 2 degrees
